cover.title: Sites
p3s1i0: This screen manages the sites that recruit subjects for this project. Each site has a principal investigator and IRB approval information, and you assign investigators to work at that site. You can register subjects only after sites exist, so this is setup work that must be finished before subject registration.
p3.cap.1: Site list (SCR-PRJ-005) — new registration is closed because the project is active
p3s2i0: Search — Narrows the rows by principal investigator name.
p3s2i1: Status filter — Narrows the rows to Active or Closed.
p3s2i2: Register — Moves to the Investigator assignment screen for that site 3.1. The number on the left is the number of investigators currently assigned.
p3s2i3: Row actions — There are two: Edit 2.3 and Investigator assignment 3.1. There is no option to close a site here, because all sites under the project are closed automatically when you close the project.
p3s2i4: Subject count — Select it to go to the subject list for that site.
p3s2i5: The path is Dashboard / Project settings / Sites.
p3s2i6: The number in parentheses next to the title is the number of registered sites.
p3s2i7: Yellow banner — “Current project status: “Active.” New sites can be registered only in Setup or Test status.” When this banner appears, the register button is not shown 1.2.
p3s2i8: List · Summary view tabs — The summary view shows each site's registration status as cards. Auditors cannot view the summary view.
p3s2i9: Site code · Site name — The site code is not the site's own code. It is a number assigned within this project (siteCode) 1.2. The small text under the site name is the code from the site master.
p3s2i11: Principal investigator — Shows the name entered on the register or edit screen as-is.
p3s2i12: IRB approval date / Approval number — The approval number is optional, so if it is empty, — is shown.
p3s3.name: Other ways to reach this screen
p3s3i1: Shortcut to Sites on the project settings screen
p3s3i2: Shortcut to Investigator assignment on the project settings screen (opens with the investigator count column highlighted)
p3s3i3: A row in the Sites widget on the project dashboard, or View all
p3s4i0: A principal investigator (PI) can edit and assign only the rows for their own site. No action menu appears on rows for other sites. Research nurses, monitors and auditors can only read the list.
p4.title: When registration is available
p4s1i0: This is the same screen as on the previous page, opened for a different project. This project is still in Setup, so there is no yellow banner, and the Register site button appears at the top right. Sites can be added or edited only in Setup or Test stages, so finalize the site setup before you start live operation.
p4.cap.1: Same screen, but for a project in Setup — the banner disappears and the register button appears
p4s2i0: + Register site — Adds a new site 2.1. It appears only when the project is in Setup or Test, and only for people with permission.
p4s2i1: Register — Moves to the investigator assignment screen 3.1.
p4s2i2: Under the title, the project name and protocol number are shown. Check here that this is a different project from the one on the previous page.
p4s2i3: The List and Summary view tabs are the same regardless of project status.
p4s2i4: The site code is the same value as the site master code. This is because if you leave the site number blank when you register, the site code is entered as-is. As on the previous page, you can also set it yourself in the SITE-01 format.
p4s2i5: Principal investigator is a free-text field, so a value that is not a real name is also shown as entered.
p4s2i6: IRB approval number left blank — It is optional, so — is shown. The IRB approval date is required.
p4s2i7: Subject count — Subjects registered during Setup are test data, and all of them are deleted when live operation starts.
p4s3.name: What is allowed by project status
p4s3r1c1: Not allowed — Banner shown · input fields disabled
p4s4i0: Once live operation starts, you cannot add any more sites. In contrast, investigator assignment stays possible during operation, because replacing staff is normal work. Do not remember these two as the same restriction. Before you switch to live operation, confirm that all the sites that will take part have been added.

ch2.title: Register and edit sites
sec2.1.title: Select site
sec2.2.title: Request site registration
sec2.3.title: Edit screen
p5s1i0: This is the first step in adding a site. You do not type in a new site. Instead, you select it from the list of sites already registered. After you select a site, fields for site number · principal investigator name · IRB approval information follow below it (for the field layout, see 2.3).
p5.cap.1: Register site (SCR-PRJ-006) — first select a site from the site master
p5s2i0: Site search — Narrows the list by site name, code or country.
p5s2i1: Select site — Select a site from the list. Selecting one opens the input fields below and the Register button.
p5s2i2: + Request site registration — Use this when the site you want is not in the list 2.2.
p5s2i3: Register — Saves your input and returns to the list. It stays faded and cannot be selected until you fill in site · site number · principal investigator name · IRB approval date.
p5s2i4: ← Site list — Returns to the list without saving.
p5s2i5: Confirm which project you are adding the site to by the project name and protocol number.
p5s2i6: Site card — The area where you select a site. You cannot edit the site's own information (name, address, type) here.
p5s2i7: The small text under each item is the site code · country · English name. If sites have similar names, use these values to tell them apart.
p5s2i8: The list scrolls. The four items you can see are not all of them, so narrow it down with search to check.
p5s2i9: Cancel — Discards your input and returns to the list.
p5s3i0: If you select the wrong site, you cannot change it after registration. The site selection area itself is not shown on the edit screen 2.3. To change the site, you must register the site again, so check the code and country before you select.
p6.title: Request site registration
p6s1i0: Use this dialog when the site you want to add is not in the site list. The site is not created here right away. It appears in the list only after a system administrator reviews and approves it, and you receive a notification when it is approved. So you continue site registration after the approval.
p6.cap.1: Request site registration — request a site that is not in the list from the system administrator (enlarged)
p6s2i0: Proposed code — Required. Propose a short code to identify the site (e.g., “SNUH” · “AMC”). The administrator sets the final code.
p6s2i1: Site name — Required. Enter the official name.
p6s2i2: English name — Optional. Enter it when you need to tell sites apart in a multi-country study.
p6s2i3: Site type — Required. Select a type, such as hospital.
p6s2i4: Country — Required. The default is South Korea. Narrow the list by search and select.
p6s2i5: Reason for request — Optional. Writing the grounds for the administrator's decision speeds up the review.
p6s2i6: Submit request — Sends the request. After you submit, the dialog does not close right away. It changes to a completion notice, so check the content and then close it.
p6s2i7: Notice — “This site is not registered in Site management. You will receive a notification once the system administrator reviews and approves it.”
p6s2i8: Close — Closes the dialog without sending a request.
p6s2i9: Country input note — “ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 code (narrow by search and select).” It uses two-letter country codes, and values not in the list cannot be entered.
p6s2i10: Cancel — Discards your input and closes the dialog.
p6s3i0: If a request with the same code is already pending, the request is rejected. In that case, do not request again. Wait until the administrator's review is complete. Someone else may already have requested the same site. Until it is approved, you cannot add that site as a Site.
p7.title: Edit screen
p7s1i0: This screen edits the values of a registered site. Its input fields are the same as on the register screen, but you cannot change the site itself. The capture shows an Active project, so every field is disabled. In the Setup · Test stages, you can edit and save the values in the same place.
p7.cap.1: Edit site — every input field is disabled because the project is active
p7s2i0: Site number (siteCode) — The number that identifies this site within the project. It cannot be changed once even one subject is registered.
p7s2i1: Principal investigator name — Required. It is shown as-is in the principal investigator column of the list.
p7s2i3: IRB approval number — Optional. If left blank, — is shown in the list.
p7s2i4: Status — Select Active or Closed. A principal investigator cannot change this field.
p7s2i5: Save — Applies the changes and returns to the list.
p7s2i6: Yellow banner — “Sites can be registered and edited only when PRJ status = SETUP / TESTING.” The part in parentheses shows the current status. When this banner appears, you cannot save.
p7s2i7: Site information cannot be edited on this screen — The site's name, type and country are changed only on the Site management screen. What you change here is only the participation terms for this project.
p7s2i8: The selected site name and site code — On the edit screen, you cannot switch to a different site.
p7s2i9: The label also shows the reason for the lock: “Subject exists — cannot be changed.” This field stays locked even when a principal investigator edits it.
p7s2i10: Cancel — Discards the changes and returns to the list.
p7s3i0: The site number is fixed for good as soon as a subject exists, because the subject identification numbers already issued include this number. If you want to change the numbering scheme, finish it before you register any subjects.
p8.title: Assignment status
ch3.title: Investigator assignment
sec3.1.title: Assignment status
sec3.2.title: Add investigator
sec3.3.title: Assignment rules
p8s1i0: This screen is where you decide who works at each site. Each site has its own tab, and the investigators assigned to that site are listed inside the tab. You can keep assigning investigators during live operation, because replacing staff is normal work that happens while the study is running.
p8.cap.1: Investigator assignment (SCR-PRJ-007) — a separate tab for each site
p8s2i0: Add investigator — Assigns a person to this site 3.2.
p8s2i1: Site tabs — If there are several sites, they are split into tabs. A principal investigator sees only the tab for their own site.
p8s2i2: Release — Removes the assignment. You can run it only after you enter a reason of at least 5 characters. The confirmation dialog explains the scope of the impact 3.3.
p8s2i3: The path is Dashboard / Project settings / Sites / Investigator assignment.
p8s2i4: Change history — Cannot be selected at the moment. Assignment and release records are kept in the system, and the screen for viewing them is being prepared.
p8s2i5: The site number · site name · principal investigator of the selected site. Before you work, check here which site you are looking at.
p8s2i6: Role — The role the person holds at this site 3.3.
p8s2i7: Assigned date — The date and time of the assignment.
p8s2i8: Status — Active or Released. A person who has been released does not disappear from the list. They remain listed as Released.
p8s2i9: Email — Use this value to tell people apart when several have the same name.
p8s3i0: Releasing does not erase the record. It is not physical deletion but deactivation, and the data and signatures that person entered up to that point remain as they are. This is because clinical trial data must stay traceable to who did what and when.
p9.title: Add investigator
p9s1i0: This dialog assigns a person to the selected site. You cannot pick just anyone; you choose only from users who already belong to the workspace. After you choose a person and a role and select Assign, it takes effect immediately.
p9.cap.1: Add investigator — select from workspace members (enlarged)
p9s2i0: Search — Narrows the list by email or name.
p9s2i1: Select user — Select one person from the list. A person already assigned to this site is marked Already assigned and cannot be selected.
p9s2i2: Role — Select the role this person will hold at this site. The only roles you can choose are the three roles that work at the site level 3.3.
p9s2i3: Reason for assignment — Optional. For an assignment with a background, such as a replacement or added staff, writing it down makes it easier to check later.
p9s2i4: Assign — Applies the assignment. It stays faded and cannot be selected until you choose both a person and a role.
p9s2i6: Notice — “Only users assigned to the workspace are searched. If the person is not listed, add them first on the Workspace user management screen.”
p9s2i7: The small text under each item is the email. If several people have the same name, use this value to tell them apart.
p9s2i8: The list scrolls. The few items you see are not all of them, so narrow it down with search to check.
p9s3i0: If the person you are looking for is not in the list, they are not yet a workspace member. You cannot create an account in this dialog, so add them first on the Workspace user management screen, and then come back. Searching with a different name will not make them appear.
p10.title: Assignment rules
p10s1i0: Below the assignment screen, a card shows which roles can be assigned. There are two rules: only roles that work at the site level can be assigned, and one person is assigned to only one site in one project. The system enforces both rules, so an assignment that breaks them is not saved.
p10.cap.1: Role permissions summary below the screen — the two assignment rules are written here
p10s2i0: Role permissions summary — Lists all roles defined for this project. Whether a role can be assigned is shown by the Site restriction label below.
p10s2i1: Roles without the Site restriction label (auditor · data manager) see all sites together, so they are not assigned to a specific site. These roles are granted at the project level on the Role management screen.
p10s2i2: Site restriction — A label for roles that handle only their own site. In the role list of the Add investigator dialog, only roles with this label appear.
p10s2i3: The on-screen notice states both rules as they are: “Only Site-restricted roles can be assigned. One investigator can be assigned to only one Site within a project (UNIQUE constraint).”
p10s3.name: Five roles and whether they can be assigned
p10s3r0c1: Is responsible for the subjects and data at their own site
p10s3r1c1: Enters subject data for their own site
p10s3r2c1: Checks the data for their own site against source data
p10s3r3c1: Manages data from all sites together
p10s3r4c1: Reviews all sites in read-only mode
p10s4i0: Releasing an assignment also removes that person's role in the project. Site assignment and role assignment move together, so to move a person to another site, you must first release them and then assign them again at the new site. You cannot assign someone to two sites at the same time.
